before.stem: ww A direct inguinal hernia is due to weakness in which of the following layers:
before.explanation: A direct inguinal hernia is due to weakness in the posterior wall of the inguinal canal which is formed mainly by the transversalis fascia. Vv

after.stem: A direct inguinal hernia is due to weakness in which of the following layers:
warnings: Source page and external anatomy reference reviewed; remains an unapproved OCR draft.
after.explanation: A direct inguinal hernia passes through acquired weakness in the posterior wall of the inguinal canal, where transversalis fascia is the key layer.
after.learningNote: A direct inguinal hernia passes through acquired weakness in the posterior wall of the inguinal canal, where transversalis fascia is the key layer.
after.highYieldNote: A direct inguinal hernia passes through acquired weakness in the posterior wall of the inguinal canal, where transversalis fascia is the key layer.
after.mnemonic: Direct goes through a defective posterior wall.

memoryAid.coreFact: Direct inguinal hernia reflects posterior-wall weakness, particularly at transversalis fascia.
memoryAid.mnemonic: Direct goes through a defective posterior wall.

evidence.externalFinding: NCBI describes direct hernia through posterior inguinal-canal wall weakness and identifies the transversalis layer in the posterior wall.

before.stem: ww The following structures are all found in the spermatic cord EXCEPT for the:
before.explanation: The pudendal nerve is not a component of the spermatic cord. Vv

after.stem: The following structures are all found in the spermatic cord EXCEPT for the:
warnings: Source page and external anatomy reference reviewed; remains an unapproved OCR draft.
after.explanation: The pudendal nerve is an S2–S4 perineal nerve rather than a spermatic-cord content.
after.learningNote: The pudendal nerve is an S2–S4 perineal nerve rather than a spermatic-cord content.
after.highYieldNote: The pudendal nerve is an S2–S4 perineal nerve rather than a spermatic-cord content.

before.stem: wy A565 year old woman presents to ED complaining of abdominal pain and profuse vomiting. Imaging shows part of the bowel is being compressed between the abdominal aorta and the superior mesenteric artery. Which part of the bowel is most likely being affected:
options: First part of the duodenum 17% (/) Third part of the duodenum 48%
warnings: No marked correct option was detected.
before.explanation: The third part of the duodenum lies anterior to the abdominal aorta but posterior to the superior mesenteric artery and constriction between these structures can occur readily. : : Vv

after.stem: A 55 year old woman presents to ED complaining of abdominal pain and profuse vomiting. Imaging shows part of the bowel is being compressed between the abdominal aorta and the superior mesenteric artery. Which part of the bowel is most likely being affected:
warnings: Source page and external anatomy reference reviewed; remains an unapproved OCR draft.
after.explanation: Superior mesenteric artery syndrome compresses the third part of the duodenum between the aorta posteriorly and the superior mesenteric artery anteriorly.
after.learningNote: Superior mesenteric artery syndrome compresses the third part of the duodenum between the aorta posteriorly and the superior mesenteric artery anteriorly.
after.highYieldNote: Superior mesenteric artery syndrome compresses the third part of the duodenum between the aorta posteriorly and the superior mesenteric artery anteriorly.
after.mnemonic: SMA squeezes D3 against the aorta.

memoryAid.coreFact: The third duodenum lies in the aortomesenteric angle and is compressed in SMA syndrome.
memoryAid.mnemonic: SMA squeezes D3 against the aorta.
memoryAid.sourceLabel: NCBI Bookshelf: Superior Mesenteric Artery Syndrome

evidence.externalFinding: NCBI states that SMA syndrome compresses the third part of the duodenum between the aorta and SMA.

before.stem: The inferior vena cava leaves the abdomen at which of the following vertebral levels:
warnings: No marked correct option was detected.
before.explanation: The inferior vena cava ascends through the posterior abdominal region anterior to the vertebral column immediately to the right of the abdominal aorta, and continues superiorly, leaving the abdomen by piercing the diaphragm at the level of vertebra T8. ; Vv

after.stem: The inferior vena cava leaves the abdomen at which of the following vertebral levels:
warnings: Source page and external anatomy reference reviewed; remains an unapproved OCR draft.
after.explanation: The inferior vena cava passes through the central tendon of the diaphragm at approximately T8.
after.learningNote: The inferior vena cava passes through the central tendon of the diaphragm at approximately T8.
after.highYieldNote: The inferior vena cava passes through the central tendon of the diaphragm at approximately T8.
after.mnemonic: IVC at 8, oesophagus at 10, aorta at 12.

memoryAid.coreFact: The IVC crosses the diaphragm through the caval opening at approximately T8.
memoryAid.mnemonic: IVC at 8, oesophagus at 10, aorta at 12.

evidence.externalFinding: NCBI states that the IVC passes through the central diaphragm tendon around T8.

before.stem: Abdomen A75 year old man presents to ED complaining of abdominal pain radiating to his back, anorexia and weight loss. Imaging shows a large tumour of the neck of the pancreas. Which of the following structures is most likely compressed by the tumour:
warnings: No marked correct option was detected.
before.explanation: The portal vein is formed from the union of the superior mesenteric and splenic veins posterior to the neck of the pancreas and would most likely be compressed by a tumour at this location.

after.stem: A 75 year old man presents to ED complaining of abdominal pain radiating to his back, anorexia and weight loss. Imaging shows a large tumour of the neck of the pancreas. Which of the following structures is most likely compressed by the tumour:
warnings: Source page and external anatomy reference reviewed; remains an unapproved OCR draft.
after.explanation: The portal vein forms posterior to the pancreatic neck from the splenic and superior mesenteric veins, making it vulnerable to a neck mass.
after.learningNote: The portal vein forms posterior to the pancreatic neck from the splenic and superior mesenteric veins, making it vulnerable to a neck mass.
after.highYieldNote: The portal vein forms posterior to the pancreatic neck from the splenic and superior mesenteric veins, making it vulnerable to a neck mass.
after.mnemonic: Portal vein sits behind the pancreatic neck.

memoryAid.coreFact: The portal vein forms behind the neck of the pancreas from the splenic and superior mesenteric veins.
memoryAid.mnemonic: Portal vein sits behind the pancreatic neck.
memoryAid.sourceLabel: PMC: Portal Venous System and Its Tributaries

evidence.externalFinding: A peer-reviewed review states that the portal vein forms behind the neck of the pancreas.

options: The anterior superior iliac spine to the sacrum and coccyx (x) jac spine to the sacrum and coccyx 20%
The ischial tuberosity to the sacrum and coccyx "1%
The pubic arch to the sacrum and coccyx

before.explanation: The sacrospinous ligament is triangular with its apex attached to the ischial spine and its base attached to the related margins of the sacrum and coccyx. Vv

after.stem: The sacrospinous ligament spans between which of the following structures:
options: The anterior superior iliac spine to the sacrum and coccyx
The posterior superior iliac spine to the sacrum and coccyx
The ischial tuberosity to the sacrum and coccyx
The ischial spine to the sacrum and coccyx
The pubic arch to the sacrum and coccyx

after.explanation: The sacrospinous ligament has a broad attachment to the lower sacrum and upper coccyx and narrows to the ischial spine.

before.stem: Abdomen The quadratus |umborum muscle is innervated by which of the following:
warnings: No marked correct option was detected.
before.explanation: The quadratus lumborum muscles are innervated by the anterior rami of T12 and L1 - L4. Vv

evidence.externalFinding: NCBI names the 12th thoracic intercostal, iliohypogastric, and ilioinguinal nerves for quadratus lumborum innervation.

before.stem: Abdomen Visceral afferent fibres from the pancreas travel to which of the following spinal cord levels:
warnings: No marked correct option was detected.
before.explanation: Visceral afferent fibres travel in the greater and lesser splanchnic nerves. The segmental level of innervation is T6 - T10. Pain typically radiates to the middle of the back due to irritation of the parietal peritoneum covering the pancreas. Vv

after.stem: Visceral afferent fibres from the pancreas travel to which of the following spinal cord levels:
warnings: Source page reviewed, but a pancreas-specialist reference places pancreatic spinal afferent neuron cell bodies at T6-L2, conflicting with the source's unqualified T6-T10 visceral-afferent range; no answer is inferred.
after.explanation: Pancreapedia reports pancreatic spinal afferent neuron cell bodies in T6-L2 dorsal root ganglia.

evidence.externalFinding: Pancreapedia reports pancreatic spinal afferent neuron cell bodies in T6-L2 dorsal root ganglia.
